angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 537,776 km at 42.75 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.3945 +/- 0.0185 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 42.75 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.773 +/- 0.023 solar radii from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5800 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...701A..79N/abstract): 537,776 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.778 +/- 0.037 solar masses from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5800 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...701A..79N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4850 +/- 78 K from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5800 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...701A..79N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5800 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...701A..79N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5800.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.553, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
